thesis.v: Former Carter Bank & Trust branch on a signalized corner of 5th Street SW — a 0.90-acre (39,248 SF) lot with a GIS building footprint of roughly 3,240 SF, close to I-64 and the 5th Street Station retail node (Wegmans). This is the highest-density one-mile residential ring of the three Goodwill sites under review (13,959 residents, roughly 3.3x Mill Creek's), and its 19,000 ADT site frontage sits inside a corridor that thickens to 28,000 ADT just south toward 5th Street Station. Two real open questions: the building is likely well under the 10,260 SF Goodwill occupies at its Mill Creek store, so total usable area (including any upstairs space) needs confirming before this is compared to a full-format store; and the parcel's CX-8 zoning permits far more density than the ~8% lot coverage currently built, which matters if redevelopment rather than reuse ends up on the table. Trade area overlaps materially with the existing Mill Creek/Avon store (1.6 miles apart) — cannibalization is a real open question. No financing model or development scenario has been built for this site yet — this card is basic property information only, per Ben's 8/19 request.

flags.text: Highest one-mile population and household density of the three sites under review (13,959 residents, 5,635 households) — about 3.3x Mill Creek's one-mile population.
Signalized corner with an intact drive-thru — a Goodwill donation drive-through could reuse the existing lane rather than requiring new site work.
Close to I-64 and the 5th Street Station shopping center (Wegmans-anchored) — the corridor thickens to 28,000 ADT between I-64 and the city line, versus 19,000 ADT at the site's own frontage.

CX-8 zoning (Commercial Mixed Use, up to 8 stories) permits substantially more density than what's built — the 0.90-acre lot sits at roughly 8% building coverage today. Relevant if redevelopment rather than reuse ends up on the table.

Answers Jackson Green's (Goodwill CFO) 8/19 diligence question directly: 5th St SW carries 19,000 ADT / 21,000 weekday at the site frontage, roughly 70% heavier than the 11,000–12,000 ADT on Avon St Ext at Mill Creek.

SIZE CONSTRAINT: the City GIS building footprint is roughly 3,240 SF. Even with the upstairs space Jackson referenced, total area is likely well under the 10,260 SF Goodwill occupies at its Mill Creek store — confirm total SF before this site is compared to a full-format store.

Trade area overlaps materially with the existing Mill Creek/Avon store — only 1.6 miles apart, sharing the same south-Charlottesville rooftops. Renter-heavy inside 1 mile (48%) and 3 miles (57%), reflecting the UVA-adjacent Fifth/Ridge neighborhoods.

Listing price ($2,595,000 asking per the active LoopNet/Triangle Realtors listing) is well above a $1,375,000 figure that appears in some property records for a prior transaction, and above the 2026 assessed value of $1,270,200 — reconcile which basis applies before underwriting.

CX-8 (Commercial Mixed Use) generally supports retail by-right; confirm Goodwill's specific use (retail + donation drive-thru) against the City's design/entrance-corridor guidelines before assuming no review is needed. Separately, CX-8's density allowance (up to 8 stories) is far beyond the single-story bank building on-site today — worth noting if redevelopment ever becomes the conversation instead of reuse.
Reuse of the existing building as a Goodwill retail store, likely retaining the drive-thru lane for donations
CX-8 zoning permits far more density (up to 8 stories) than the current ~8% lot coverage — a longer-horizon alternative to simple reuse, not something Goodwill's near-term store search needs to weigh

extras.label: Demographic methodology note
extras.text: Ring demographics (ACS 2019–2023 5-year estimates) are aggregated by block-group centroid falling inside each radius — block groups aren't split at the ring boundary, so small rings are approximate. Median household income is a household-weighted average of block-group medians, not a true ring median.
